- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent days.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment, often overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or adjust downward 1–3 days after spike.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts rise, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–5 days after bearish sentiment resumes.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction: subtract 1–3% per day for 3–5 days if sentiment remains neutral or bearish.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >1.5% daily avg), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to adjust forecast midpoint.
